risk_if_not_implemented: Without Applied Security, Compliance and Resilience Controls Documentation, executive management, the Board of Directors (BoD) and assessors may rely on inaccurate, incomplete or unverifiable control and risk information. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Authorization / Certification / License (R-EX-11), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information (R-GV-10), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12).

compensating_control_1.name: Conformity Monitoring
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to validate that Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) conform to the organization's security, compliance and/or resilience policies, standards and other applicable requirements.
compensating_control_1.justification: Conformity Monitoring (CPL-05) provides periodic assessment and assurance that compensates for the absence of Applied Security, Compliance and Resilience Controls Documentation (IAO-09) by providing structured evaluation of the environment to surface gaps and verify residual control effectiveness. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Publishing Security, Compliance & Resilience Documentation
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to establish, maintain and disseminate policies, standards and procedures necessary for secure, compliant and resilient capabilities.
compensating_control_2.justification: Publishing Security, Compliance & Resilience Documentation (GOV-04) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Applied Security, Compliance and Resilience Controls Documentation (IAO-09) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
